title: fix(metadata-core): the protocol refusal prescribes no migrate meta --from below the migration floor
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DH9e4qEZ6HPSFPqXCYcdFui)_

Fixes #33031

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:包声明的协议主版本低于迁移链下限(16)时,安装拒绝(422 `OS_PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE`)不再开出 `objectstack migrate meta --from N` 这条注定被 CLI 拒绝的命令,改为说明两条真正可行的补救:装一个针对本运行时协议的包构建,或先经其他途径升到 16 再 `--from 16`。
- **为什么改**:作者照着 422 提示去跑命令,CLI 立刻回"链的支持下限是 16",诊断自相矛盾;版本高于运行时的分支早已这样处理,本次让低于下限的分支对齐。
- **风险与回滚**:只动诊断:低于 16 时 `details.migrateCommand` 缺省、文案换成补救说明;状态码、错误码、准入判定和 16 及以上的提示一字不变。回滚即还原这一个提交。已知一处他包测试(`packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.test.ts`)断言了 `--from 13`,正是本缺陷的旧行为,需随本 PR 改一行断言(超出派发文件面,已上报席位)。
- **先看**:① `packages/metadata-core/src/protocol-handshake.ts` 的 `belowFloor` 分支与文件顶部 `MIGRATE_META_SUPPORT_FLOOR` 常量(为何不直接 import 见下文);② 同目录 `protocol-handshake.test.ts` 末尾新增的 describe 与被改写的旧 fixture;③ changeset。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-core exec vitest run src/protocol-handshake.test.ts`,预期 56 个测试全部通过。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地。

## What changes

`checkProtocolCompat` (`packages/metadata-core/src/protocol-handshake.ts`) built `migrateCommand = objectstack migrate meta --from TARGET` for every declared major that is not ahead of the runtime, with no floor check. The CLI's chain refuses every `--from N` under `MIGRATION_SUPPORT_FLOOR` (16, ADR-0087 D3; `MigrationFloorError`), so a manifest declaring `engines.protocol: '^15'` or `'^0'` was told to run a command known to fail.

Below the floor the refusal now mirrors the AHEAD arm (#26480): no `migrateCommand` member (so no `details.migrateCommand` on the HTTP answer), and the message names the remedies that apply. Built output on an 18 runtime:

```text
^15 -> migrateCommand: (absent)
  ... This is a major-version break. The package is built for protocol 15, older than the oldest protocol objectstack migrate meta replays from (16, ADR-0087 D3). Install a build of 'com.example.qa-floor' for protocol 18, or bring its metadata to protocol 16 by another path first and then migrate it with objectstack migrate meta --from 16
^0  -> same shape, "built for protocol 0"
^16 -> migrateCommand: objectstack migrate meta --from 16   (unchanged, ends "Run: objectstack migrate meta --from 16")
^17 -> migrateCommand: objectstack migrate meta --from 17   (unchanged)
```

Choices made on the dispatch's axes (author-facing correctness, then smallest public surface, then effort):

- **Omitted, not replaced with `--from 16`.** `--from 16` on protocol-15 metadata runs: it starts at the floor, never replays the hops below it, and `--write` still moves the declared range (`planProtocolRange` in the CLI presumes the floor was reached another way). As a machine-actionable `migrateCommand` it would hand an agent a run that reports success over metadata it never migrated. The prose keeps the conditional path for a human.
- **The `details` shape does not change.** `migrateCommand` was already optional on `ProtocolIncompatibleDiagnostic` and `ProtocolIncompatibleAnswer.details`, and already absent on the AHEAD arm; no member is added or dropped, only the set of cases where the optional one is present shrinks. Status 422 and code `OS_PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE` are unchanged. Hence `Clause-②: no`; the open question is recorded in the os-dev report.
- **The floor is spelled locally (`MIGRATE_META_SUPPORT_FLOOR = 16`), not imported.** `MIGRATION_SUPPORT_FLOOR` lives only on `@objectstack/spec/migrations`, whose built entry is about 2.9 MB (the migration registry, split off the spec root for exactly this reason) and measured at +11 MB heap on load. `metadata-core` is reached by every install door and by browser bundles (`@object-ui/app-shell`), so importing it to read one number is the wrong trade. The test file imports the spec's constant and sweeps majors 0 to floor+2, so a release-policy ruling that moves the spec floor reds this package until the copy follows (ablation below).

## Tests

- New `describe('[#33031] ...')` in `protocol-handshake.test.ts`: below the floor (`^15`, `^0`, a union whose lowest alternative is 15) carries no `migrateCommand`, never offers `--from N` or a `Run:` line, and names the build for protocol 18 and the floor; AT the floor `^16` keeps `--from 16`; CONTROL `^17` keeps `--from 17` and an undeterminable target keeps the bare command; the HTTP answer for `^15` carries the four applicable members and still declares 422; a sweep pins the local floor equal to the spec's `MIGRATION_SUPPORT_FLOOR`.
- Fixture triage: existing pins that prescribed `--from` under the floor (`--from 10`, `--from 6` on an 11 runtime; `>=15 <18` on 18) pinned the defect itself. They are re-spelled onto an above-floor runtime (`RT_ABOVE_FLOOR = '18.0.0'`, or 21 for the one-or-five-behind shape test) so each keeps asserting what it was written for.

## Acceptance notes

- **Known red outside this dispatch's file surface:** `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.test.ts` ("refuses an incompatible engines.protocol range BEFORE registering the manifest") declares `^(PROTOCOL_MAJOR - 5)` = `^13` and asserts `migrateCommand: objectstack migrate meta --from 13`, the very prescription this card removes. Measured red on this branch (1 failed, 83 passed across the three runtime protocol suites). The one-line fix is to assert `targetMajor: PROTOCOL_MAJOR - 5` instead (the seam's point is that the diagnostic arrives before registration; which remedy it names is metadata-core's pin). Not edited here: the file surface is `metadata-core` plus one changeset, and that edit is the seat's to authorize.
- The platform checklist clause for `platform-core.manifest-install-contract` (`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/platform-core.json`, acceptance[1]) still says every target at or below the runtime carries a `migrateCommand`; it now holds only from the floor up. Checklist accuracy follow-up, not edited here.
- `MIGRATE_META_SUPPORT_FLOOR` is a second spelling of the spec's number, held by a test rather than an import. A lighter spec export of the floor (for example beside `PROTOCOL_VERSION` on `@objectstack/spec/kernel`) would remove the copy; that is a spec public-surface addition and out of this card's surface.

## Verification

</details>

The full affected set (108 packages by `select-shard-packages.sh`) is Test Core's in CI.
</details>

</details>
